title: Sample Cutting and Processing Protocol
author: Khai-Minh H Nguyen
materials: Download new Barcode Processing Template Bar_Code Processing Template.xlsx
Wipe gloved hands with RNAse Zap Wipes

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Samples
steps.instruction: Prepare the cooling environment and thaw the samples.

substeps.instruction: Fill an insulated foam box with dry ice and place an empty tube rack inside to chill.
Place 16 samples on the tube rack in two rows of 8 and allow them to thaw for 00:15:00.

steps.title: Prepare Documentation and Labeling
steps.instruction: Set up the tracking and storage labeling system.

substeps.instruction: Label a new processed sample box (cryo freezer box 2'', 89 slots) using the format: (PI Name) processed Box ##, Date, Initials of Lab Tech, Project.
In the barcode processing excel sheet, enter the name of the shipping box in Column A ('Origin').
Scan and enter transponder IDs (A1-H1 for the first row, A2-H2 for the second row); enter 'no transponder' in comments if the chip does not scan.
Scan barcodes in the same order as transponders (A1-H1 for the first row); enter 'no barcode' in comments if missing and note the written code on the tube.

Verify matches between transponder IDs and barcodes. If a barcode is a truncated version of the transponder ID, use the formula =IF(TEXT(C2, "0")=CONCATENATE("000", TEXT(D2, "0")), "PASS", "FAIL") to check for a match. Mark any 'FAIL' as a mismatch.

steps.title: Prepare Cutting Station
steps.instruction: Set up and sterilize the cutting area.

substeps.instruction: Fill an ice pan with ice and chill a metal cutting block.
Fill a wash bottle with 70% EtOH.
Clean and spray the metal cutting block, razor, and tweezers with 70% EtOH and Kimwipes (use a 100mL waste beaker for ethanol waste).

steps.title: Tissue Sampling
steps.instruction: Extract specific tissue amounts from the samples while maintaining order.

substeps.instruction: Using a razor and tweezers, cut a small section of sample and place it into the corresponding well of a deepwell plate (Catalog AB0932).
Target weights: Spleen tissue = 5-6 mg; Tail = 8-10 mg.
Maintain the order from the barcode processing sheet (Check wells A1, B1, C1).
Note in the comments section if the spleen does not appear healthy (healthy spleens should be intact/firm and vibrant deep red).
Immediately return the remaining tissue to the tube and place it back on the tube rack on dry ice.
Repeat the cutting and return process for all 16 samples.

steps.title: Lysis Buffer Addition
steps.instruction: Add lysis buffer to the processed tissue samples.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL of Lysis Buffer (Beckman Coulter Catalog #A48706) to each well of the deepwell plate using a reagent reservoir and a multichannel pipette.
Place the deepwell plate on ice.
Label the side of the plate with the DNA plate code (e.g., John03), the date, and your initials.

steps.title: Sample Storage and Final Logging
steps.instruction: Store the samples and finalize the extraction database.

substeps.instruction: Place processed samples in the labeled box, maintaining the scanned order.
Enter the storage sample box name in column G and sample position in column H of the barcode processing excel sheet.
Store processed samples in a -80°C freezer.
Enter the tissue type (typically spleen or tail) in column J of the processing sheet.
Create a new extraction database on Google Sheets using the template, creating a separate sheet for each new plate.
Assign a DNA plate code name (e.g., 'PI Name ##' such as John03) and rename the barcode processing template excel sheet with this code.

Populate the extraction database: Column A (DNA plate code), Columns D and E (Transponder IDs and Barcodes), Column K (Origin), Column M (Tissue Type), Columns N and O (Storage Box and Position), Column Q (Comments), and Column P (Freezer location of the processed sample box).
